coverage_notes: Sections 7.1(b), 7.1(c), and 7.2 contain liability allocations, dispute-release terms, and enforcement powers or duties that do not faithfully fit the fixed activity vocabulary. The previously recovered Use clauses for those provisions are not treated as activity constraints.
Section 7.3 (line 145) is a limitation-of-liability provision, not an activity constraint.

paragraph_audit.reason: Section 7.1(b) allocates joint and several liability for losses or damage to DeepSeek arising from end-user breaches. Liability allocation is not an action expressible with the fixed activities; the recovered Use clause does not represent it faithfully.

Section 7.1(c) allocates end-user disputes to the licensee and end user and releases DeepSeek to the extent permitted by law. Dispute resolution and release are not expressible with the fixed activities; the recovered Use clause does not represent them faithfully.

Section 7.2(a) states a trigger for DeepSeek's discretionary enforcement powers based on suspected or determined breach. Those provider enforcement powers do not fit the fixed activities; this is not a licensee Use constraint.

Section 7.2(b) states a trigger for DeepSeek's discretionary enforcement powers based on service disruption or significant threat. Those provider enforcement powers do not fit the fixed activities; this is not a licensee Use constraint.

Section 7.2(c) makes breach of payment obligations a trigger for DeepSeek's discretionary enforcement measures. The provider's enforcement power does not fit the fixed activities; the paragraph does not impose a new payment duty.

Section 7.2 provides DeepSeek discretionary enforcement and restoration rights, and requires DeepSeek to retain relevant records, report suspected violations or illegal activities as required by law, and cooperate with investigations. It also assigns liability and compensation for specified losses. These enforcement, reporting, retention, cooperation, and compensation actions do not fit the fixed activities.
Section 7.3 allocates and caps liability for specified damages; it does not impose an activity constraint.
